short: The TATA box is the oldest known eukaryotic core promoter element and the binding site of TBP, the TATA-box-binding protein. TBP is a saddle-shaped, internally pseudo-symmetric protein that straddles about eight base pairs of AT-rich DNA, reads them entirely from the minor groove, kinks the duplex at both ends and bends it by roughly 80 degrees. It works within TFIID for RNA polymerase II and within SL1 and TFIIIB for polymerases I and III, so a single protein serves all three. Because minor-groove contacts barely distinguish A:T from T:A, the element carries little information: the canonical TATAWAWR is present in only a small minority of human promoters, most of which are instead GC-rich and TATA-less. A TATA match on its own is therefore very weak evidence of anything.
long:
## The factors

TBP is a single small protein, about 180 residues in its conserved core, encoded by one gene. Its
fold is a pseudo-symmetric saddle: two structurally similar halves, each contributing a curved
beta sheet that forms the concave underside, with helices on the convex top surface where general
factors and activators dock. TBP does not act alone. For RNA polymerase II it is the anchoring
subunit of TFIID, a roughly one-megadalton complex of thirteen or more TAF subunits; for
polymerase I it sits in SL1 and for polymerase III in TFIIIB. Two paralogues exist, TBPL1
(TRF2/TLF) and TBPL2 (TRF3), which have the TBP fold but altered DNA-contacting surfaces and do
not bind TATA boxes; neither has a motif in the databases used here. TAF1, the largest TFIID
subunit, is included in this key because its motif models are attributed to a promoter-binding
component of the same machinery, but TAF1 is not a sequence-specific DNA-binding protein in the
way TBP is: its promoter contacts involve the initiator and downstream regions, and it carries
histone-acetyltransferase and bromodomain activities.

## The motif

The literature consensus is the eight-base TATAWAWR, most often realized as TATAAAAG or TATATAAG,
positioned roughly 25-30 bp upstream of the transcription start site in a focused promoter. The
co-crystal structures of human and yeast TBP on TATA DNA showed why the information content is
low: TBP makes no major-groove base contacts at all. It binds the minor groove, where an A:T and a
T:A base pair present nearly the same pattern of hydrogen-bond acceptors, and inserts pairs of
phenylalanine side chains between the first two and last two base pairs, kinking the helix at both
ends and bending the whole element by about 80 degrees while partially unwinding it. What TBP
really reads is a short run of deformable, narrow-minor-groove AT-rich DNA, and later work showed
that a wide range of AT-rich variants are bound with comparable affinity. The consequence for
motif models is direct: every matrix in this family is a low-information AT-rich model. The
representative here, the Vierstra archetype AC0057, is TATAAAAG; JASPAR MA0108.3 is TATAAAA;
HOCOMOCO's TBP model is CTATAAAAGG. There is no half-site structure and no spacing rule, and
because TBP is a monomer on a pseudo-symmetric site, orientation is only weakly determined by
sequence, which is one reason TATA-box orientation prediction is unreliable. Family cohesion here
is only 0.64, and two of the five motifs are flagged as belonging elsewhere, discussed below.

## Where it acts

TATA boxes belong to focused, or sharp-initiation, promoters: a single dominant start site,
AT-rich surroundings, no CpG island. These are a minority of mammalian promoters. A genome-scale
analysis found that about 76% of human core promoters have no TATA-like element, are GC-rich and
are enriched for SP1 sites; about 24% have something TATA-like, but only about 10% of those match
the canonical TATAWAWR, which puts canonical TATA boxes at a few percent of human genes. Broad,
dispersed-initiation promoters in CpG islands dominate the mammalian genome, and these use the
initiator, downstream elements and TFIID-DNA contacts rather than a TATA box. Functionally the
split is informative: TATA-less promoters skew toward housekeeping genes, while TATA-containing
promoters are enriched for highly regulated, stimulus-responsive and tissue-specific genes,
including many that are strongly induced by stress or hormones. Cryo-EM structures of
promoter-bound TFIID show TBP being loaded onto the TATA region while other TAFs contact the
initiator and downstream promoter, so the TATA box is one anchor point in an extended,
multi-contact interaction rather than the sole determinant of where transcription starts.

## Biology and disease

TBP is essential in every organism tested; there is no viable null. Its N-terminal region in
humans contains a polyglutamine tract, and expansion of that tract to roughly 43 repeats or more
causes spinocerebellar ataxia type 17, a rare autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder,
placing TBP among the polyglutamine diseases. Mutations in individual TAFs cause developmental
syndromes and intellectual disability, and TAF1 variants are associated with X-linked
neurodevelopmental disease. TATA-box variants in individual promoters cause disease in their own
right, the classic cases being promoter mutations that reduce beta-globin expression in
beta-thalassemia and the TATA-box polymorphism in the UGT1A1 promoter that contributes to
Gilbert syndrome.

## Reading a hit

Treat a TATA match as almost no evidence. TATAWAWR is an eight-base AT-rich pattern with two
degenerate positions, expected by chance roughly once every few kilobases on either strand, which
is hundreds of thousands of matches in a human genome, the overwhelming majority of them nowhere
near a promoter. A match is only interesting if it sits 25-30 bp upstream of an annotated or
measured start site in a promoter that otherwise looks focused and AT-rich. It also says nothing
about TBP itself, since TBP is present at essentially all active promoters, including TATA-less
ones, where it is positioned by TFIID rather than by sequence. This family is also a good place to
see what happens when a ChIP-derived matrix is assigned to the wrong protein. The HOCOMOCO model
TAF1.H14CORE.0.P.B is AAGATGGCGGC, which is the YY1 motif, not a TBP-like or TAF1-specific
sequence; YY1 sites are common at focused promoters, so a TAF1 ChIP experiment recovers them.
Likewise the CIS-BP TBP entry M08231_2.00 is TATTTGCATA, whose core ATTTGCAT is the POU octamer
read in reverse. Neither model should be used as a TATA box.
caveats: The TATA box is the least informative element in common use: eight AT-rich bases read entirely from the minor groove, where A:T and T:A are nearly interchangeable, so the matrix cannot be much better than the physics allows. Expect hundreds of thousands of chance matches per genome and only a few percent of human promoters to carry a real one. A match means nothing without position 25-30 bp upstream of a start site. Two of the five motifs under this key are not TATA boxes: the HOCOMOCO ChIP-derived TAF1 matrix is the YY1 motif, and the CIS-BP TBP entry M08231_2.00 is the POU octamer. Family cohesion is correspondingly low at 0.64.
